claims.claim: Eclipse Paho MQTT Rust Client supports MQTT v5, 3.1.1, and 3.1, with automatic reconnect and offline buffering built in — 'Supports MQTT v5, 3.1.1, and 3.1 ... Automatic Reconnect ... Offline Buffering'.
claims.stance_target: Paho Rust is a viable alternative to rumqttc offering MQTT v5 and automatic reconnect out of the box
claims.scope_conditions: eclipse-paho/paho.mqtt.rust README (repo migrated from eclipse org to eclipse-paho), master branch
claims.quoted_support: Supports MQTT v5, 3.1.1, and 3.1 ... Automatic Reconnect ... Offline Buffering ... High Availability

claims.claim: Paho Rust's async support is runtime-agnostic: 'Agnostic to async runtimes. Tested with tokio and smol.' and 'The library does not use a runtime for internal operations' — it wraps Paho C, using internal threads plus condition variables, with Token implementing std::future::Future.
claims.stance_target: Paho Rust is compatible with a tokio-based agent (the ha-linux-agent runtime) despite being a C wrapper
claims.scope_conditions: paho.mqtt.rust README 'A Note on Async Runtimes' and 'Features' sections
claims.quoted_support: Agnostic to async runtimes. Tested with tokio and smol. ... The library does not use a runtime for internal operations. ... To make the library compatible with the async/await paradigm, the Token simply implemented the std::future::Future trait.

claims.claim: Paho Rust is a safe wrapper around the Paho C library (v1.3.16), requiring a C compiler and CMake for the default 'bundled' build; pre-generated bindings ship for x86_64/aarch64-linux-gnu, armv7, Windows MSVC, and Apple Darwin.
claims.stance_target: Adopting paho.mqtt.rust adds a C-toolchain build dependency (CMake + C compiler + OpenSSL) that rumqttc (pure Rust) does not have
claims.quoted_support: The Rust crate is a safe wrapper around the Paho C Library. ... Requires Paho C v1.3.16, or possibly later. ... The default behaviour can be altered by enabling or disabling the features: "default" - [bundled, ssl]

claims.claim: paho.mqtt.rust v0.14.0 (released 26 Mar by fpagliughi) added synchronous and async event streams where 'All events from the client flow through the stream: Connect, Connection Lost, Disconnected, Incoming Message' — giving applications explicit connection-lost signalling that rumqttc 0.24.0 lacks.
claims.stance_target: Paho's event stream surfaces Connection Lost / Disconnected events to the application, enabling re-subscription logic without polling hacks
claims.quoted_support: Added synchronous (blocking) and async event streams. All events from the client flow through the stream: Connect, Connection Lost, Disconnected, Incoming Message
claims.time_period: v0.14.0 released 26 Mar; most recent -sys release 14 May (sys-v0.10.3)

claims.claim: Paho Rust's release cadence shows active maintenance through 2025-2026: v0.13.0 (21 Jan), v0.13.1 (19 Feb), v0.13.2 (27 Mar), v0.13.3 (28 Apr), v0.14.0 (26 Mar), sys-v0.10.3 (14 May); v0.12.3 specifically fixed 'numerous issues with reconnecting to the broker' including 'crashes on reconnect callbacks'.
claims.stance_target: paho.mqtt.rust is actively maintained and its reconnect machinery has been specifically hardened
claims.quoted_support: Upgrade to Paho C v1.3.13 to fix a number of bugs, including numerous issues with reconnecting to the broker. The -sys crate now wraps Paho C v1.3.13, fixing several issues, including crashes on reconnect callbacks.
claims.time_period: v0.12.3 (26 Oct, prior year) through sys-v0.10.3 (14 May)

claims.claim: Paho Rust v0.14.0 carries breaking changes in MQTT v5 error handling (Reason Code Error variant now contains Properties from ACK packet; ACKs with a single reason code error generate an Error result) and bumped MSRV to Rust v1.75.
claims.stance_target: Migration cost assessment for switching from rumqttc to paho.mqtt.rust
claims.quoted_support: [Breaking] Reason Code Error variant now contains Properties from ACK packet ... [Breaking] ACKs with a single reason code error generate an Error result, instead of an Ok() with a possible error code in it. ... Bumped MSRV to Rust v1.75
